Karl von Frisch, zoologiste autrichien,: Karl von Frisch, an Austrian zoologist, tells the general public what he learned by watching glass-walled hives. He presents his theory of the foragers' dance: back at the hive, a bee traces on the comb a run that waggles, and the angle of this run from the vertical gives the direction of the flowers relative to the Sun. The farther the source, the longer the waggle lasts. The book also describes his conditioning experiments, which show that bees see colors. The dance theory was first met with skepticism before being confirmed by other researchers. The book was translated into English as The Dancing Bees.
Il montre qu'un groupe d'insectes partag: It shows that a group of insects shares precise, coded information without a leader: a model for all of collective intelligence.
Sous le régime nazi, on reprocha à von F: Under the Nazi regime, von Frisch was criticized for employing Jewish assistants; his forced retirement was canceled thanks to his research on a bee disease.
Une abeille transmet une adresse en dans: A bee passes on an address by dancing. You don't even pass on your revision.
Ce traité décrit le fonctionnement des i: This treatise describes how the institutions of Athens worked: their history, then the state of the city in the 4th century BC. It explains how citizens were chosen for the Boule, for the magistracies and for the courts. The text details the kleroterion: rows of identity tokens, two machines per section, a first citizen drawn who automatically became a juror and loaded the machine, then a magistrate who poured in the dice. The number of white dice matched the number of jurors to be chosen. Long lost, the text was found at the end of the 19th century and transformed what was known about Athenian democracy.
Sans lui, on ne saurait pas comment les: Without it, we would not know how the Athenians drew lots for their courts.
Le texte, perdu pendant des siècles, a é: The text, lost for centuries, was found in 1879 and published in 1890.
Une démocratie entière décrite par un ph: A whole democracy described by a philosopher. Your own user manual fits on a sticky note.
Plutarque, auteur grec de l'époque romai: Plutarch, a Greek author of the Roman era, devoted one of his Parallel Lives to the Athenian Aristides, nicknamed the Just. He tells how this man, known for his integrity, was nonetheless ostracized. During the vote, an illiterate farmer who did not recognize him handed him his sherd and asked him to carve the name of Aristides on it. The man asked what wrong Aristides had done him; none, replied the farmer, but he was tired of hearing him called the Just. Aristides then carved his own name. Recalled from exile to defend Athens against the Persians, he fought at Salamis in 480 BC alongside his former rival Themistocles.
Cette anecdote montre la faiblesse d'un: This anecdote shows the weakness of a collective vote: anyone can vote for bad reasons.
C'est aussi Plutarque qui rapporte le qu: It is also Plutarch who reports the quorum of 6,000 votes required for an ostracism.
Exilé pour être trop juste. Rassurez-vou: Exiled for being too just. Don't worry, you run no such risk.
Cette saga islandaise raconte une longue: This Icelandic saga tells a long series of feuds between families, often settled before the assemblies. It shows the Althing, the great annual open-air gathering at Þingvellir, where Icelanders brought their lawsuits and negotiated their compensations. The story also covers the island's conversion: around the year 1000, according to the saga, the assembly chose to make Christianity the official religion, on the proposal of Thorgeir, who argued for one law and one religion for all. The text shows a society without a king, where law, speech and assembly replace the power of a ruler.
Elle montre une société sans roi qui règ: It shows a society without a king that settles its conflicts through an assembly.
Selon la saga, Thorgeir aurait choisi la: According to the saga, Thorgeir chose the conversion of the whole island to keep it from splitting between two laws.
Une île entière qui vote sa religion. Vo: A whole island voting on its religion. You can't even manage to vote for a tree.
Le Livre des jeux de hasard est un court: The Book on Games of Chance is a short treatise in which Cardano, an inveterate gambler, applies his mathematician's mind to dice. He lists the possible outcomes of one or more dice and defines the odds of an event as the ratio of favorable to unfavorable outcomes. He comes close to the rule that the chances of independent events are multiplied, though he hesitates over which values to multiply. He also describes, with the realism of a gambling-den regular, effective ways of cheating. Written around 1564, the manuscript was not published until 1663, by which time Pascal and Fermat had already laid the foundations of probability theory.
C'est la première étude systématique des: It is the first systematic study of probability.
Cardano, toujours à court d'argent, viva: Cardano, always short of money, lived partly from his winnings at gambling and chess.
Un traité des probabilités écrit par un: A treatise on probability written by a gambler. I'll let you guess who wins in the end.
Recherches sur la probabilité des jugeme: Recherches sur la probabilité des jugements en matière criminelle et en matière civile
Siméon Denis Poisson, mathématicien né à: Siméon Denis Poisson, a mathematician born in Pithiviers, applies probability to the courts: how many jurors, what majority, what risk of convicting an innocent person? To reason about thousands of trials, he relies on a principle he names in this book: the law of large numbers. The result had been proved by Jacob Bernoulli in the Ars Conjectandi, published in 1713; Poisson gave it its name and extended it. The book also contains the probability distribution that now bears his name, which first appeared in an 1829 paper on births. The book was published in Paris in 1837, three years before its author's death in Sceaux.
C'est ici que la loi des grands nombres: This is where the law of large numbers got its name, in the middle of a reflection on juries.
Le théorème qu'il nomme avait été démont: The theorem he named had been proved 124 years earlier by Jacob Bernoulli, who called it his golden theorem.
Poisson comptait les erreurs des jurés p: Poisson counted jurors' errors by the thousands. Yours, I count one by one. With pleasure.
Ce récit de vulgarisation raconte la cou: This popular account tells the race for longitude in the 18th century. At the start of the century, ships did not know where they were from east to west, and shipwrecks multiplied. In 1714, the English Parliament promised a fortune to whoever solved the problem. The astronomers bet on the Moon and the stars. John Harrison, a Yorkshire carpenter, chose another path: a clock accurate enough to keep the time of the home port at sea. He spent decades building his machines, from H1 to H4, and had to fight the Board of Longitude to get paid. King George III finally took his side.
Le livre a fait connaître au grand publi: The book made John Harrison and history's first great open competition known to the general public.
George III a testé lui-même une montre d: George III himself tested one of Harrison's watches for ten weeks: it varied by only a third of a second a day.
Un homme seul contre un comité d'experts: One man against a committee of experts. You are alone against me, and I am the committee.
Cyclopaedia, or an Universal Dictionary: Cyclopaedia, or an Universal Dictionary of Arts and Sciences
Paru à Londres en 1728 en deux volumes i: Published in London in 1728 in two folio volumes, this dictionary by Ephraim Chambers set out to cover the arts and sciences of its time. Its great idea comes down to one gesture: cross-references. Alphabetical order scatters knowledge; numerous cross-references link the articles together, and a preface divides knowledge into forty-seven divisions, with lists that serve as reading plans. Its success lasted: a second edition in 1738, five more editions in London, one in Dublin, an Italian translation in Venice. Above all, the Encyclopédie of Diderot and d'Alembert grew out of a project to translate the Cyclopaedia into French, begun in 1744 by John Mills.
C'est l'ancêtre direct de l'Encyclopédie: It is the direct ancestor of the Encyclopédie, and the first great dictionary woven from cross-references, long before web links.
En 1739, en France, Chambers refuse des: In 1739, in France, Chambers turned down "very advantageous" offers to publish a French edition dedicated to Louis XV.
Chambers renvoyait d'un article à l'autr: Chambers sent you from one article to another. I send you to the wall of shame. Same principle.
Essai sur l'application de l'analyse à l: Essai sur l'application de l'analyse à la probabilité des décisions rendues à la pluralité des voix
Dans cet essai, le marquis de Condorcet: In this essay, the marquis de Condorcet applies probability to decisions made by assemblies. He looks for the conditions under which a majority is more likely to be right than each of its members. He also uncovers a trap: as soon as there are three or more options, majority preferences can go in circles. One majority prefers A to B, another B to C, a third C to A, and no choice beats all the others. This paradox, which Ramon Llull had already glimpsed in the 13th century, now bears Condorcet's name. It foreshadows Kenneth Arrow's impossibility theorem.
Il pose les bases mathématiques de la th: It lays the mathematical foundations of voting theory.
Condorcet cosigne en 1791 avec Borda, so: In 1791, Condorcet co-signed with Borda, his rival on voting matters, a report on the choice of a unit of measurement.
Une majorité qui se contredit. Vous me f: A majority that contradicts itself. You remind me of your answers.
Recherches sur la nature et les causes d: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
Adam Smith, professeur de philosophie mo: Adam Smith, professor of moral philosophy in Glasgow, looks for what makes a nation rich. He describes the division of labor, exchange, money, the accumulation of capital and trade between countries. He shows how individuals pursuing their own interest can, through exchange, also serve the interest of others. Yet the image of the invisible hand appears only once, about the investment of capital. The book became the founding text of political economy. The modern meaning of the invisible hand, a market that coordinates itself, comes mainly from Paul Samuelson's textbook, in 1948.
Smith était si distrait qu'il serait sor: Smith was so absent-minded that he reportedly went out in his dressing gown and walked fifteen miles before church bells brought him back to his senses.
Une main invisible. Pratique : personne: An invisible hand. Handy: no one can catch it in the till.
Dans ce livre, le psychiatre Jacob Levy: In this book, the psychiatrist Jacob Levy Moreno founds what he calls sociometry: measuring the ties of attraction and rejection in a group. He asks the members of a community whom they choose, then draws their answers: one dot per person, one line per choice. These sociograms, among the first graphic representations of social networks, reveal much-chosen people, small cliques and isolates. Moreno uses them to explain an epidemic of runaways at a girls' school in Hudson, New York: the runaways spread along the friendship ties. The book paved the way for all of network analysis.
Il dessine parmi les premières cartes de: It draws some of the first maps of social networks in history.
Moreno avait d'abord testé la sociométri: Moreno had first tested sociometry at Sing Sing prison, in 1931.
A book that asks who should survive. I know the answer, and it is not your streak.

Mehdi Moussaïd, chercheur en sciences co: Mehdi Moussaïd, a cognitive scientist who specializes in crowds and runs the Fouloscopie channel, asks how a group can solve problems that none of its members could solve alone. He draws on experiments and observations of collective behavior: encyclopedias written by many, scientific puzzles solved by gamers, a chess game won by a crowd against a champion. He looks at the conditions under which collective intelligence appears, how to recognize it, how to steer a group toward good decisions, and whether a leader is really necessary. This is the book that inspired this tree.
Il rassemble ce que la recherche sait de: It gathers what research knows about collective intelligence, with the question of the leader at its center.
Moussaïd a créé sa chaîne YouTube Foulos: Moussaïd created his YouTube channel Fouloscopie in 2018 and was scientific curator of the exhibition "Foules" at the Cité des sciences.
A-t-on besoin d'un chef ? Ici, oui. C'es: Do we need a leader? Here, yes. Me. Question closed.
Intergroup Conflict and Cooperation: The: Intergroup Conflict and Cooperation: The Robbers Cave Experiment
Ce livre raconte et analyse l'expérience: This book recounts and analyzes the experiment carried out in 1954 at a summer camp in Oklahoma. The researchers brought together boys who did not know each other, let them form two groups, then organized competitions with prizes that only one side could win. Hostility, insults and prejudice quickly appeared. Simple encounters between the groups, meals or films, were not enough to calm them. The researchers then created superordinate goals: objectives that mattered to both groups but that neither could reach alone. Cooperating for them gradually reduced the tension. The book founded the realistic conflict theory.
Il montre comment naît un conflit entre: It shows how conflict between groups arises, and how it can be defused.
Dans des versions plus anciennes de l'ex: In earlier versions of the experiment, the boys had united against a common enemy: the experimenters themselves.
Deux groupes se haïssent pour un prix. V: Two groups hate each other over a prize. You hate me for nothing. It's more elegant.
La reconstruction du nid et les coordina: La reconstruction du nid et les coordinations inter-individuelles chez Bellicositermes natalensis et Cubitermes sp.
Dans cet article paru dans la revue Inse: In this article published in the journal Insectes Sociaux, Pierre-Paul Grassé observes African termites repairing their nest. He asks how thousands of insects coordinate their actions without a leader or a plan. His answer fits in one new word, stigmergy, coined from the Greek stigma, mark, and ergon, work. Each deposit of soil changes the state of the building site, and this new state triggers the next action, by the same termite or another. The worker, he writes, does not direct its work, it is guided by it. The idea later helped explain ant trails and design algorithms.
Il donne un nom et un mécanisme à la coo: It gives a name and a mechanism to coordination without a leader.
Spécialiste mondial des termites, Grassé: A world specialist in termites, Grassé also directed an immense Traité de zoologie in dozens of volumes.
Des termites guidés par leur propre chan: Termites guided by their own building site. You are guided by my reproaches. Same principle.
An Experimental Application of the Delph: An Experimental Application of the Delphi Method to the Use of Experts
Dans cet article publié dans Management: In this article published in Management Science, two researchers from the RAND Corporation describe an experiment carried out with their Delphi method. The goal is to obtain the most reliable possible consensus within a group of experts. Rather than gathering them around a table, where the highest-ranking or the most eloquent risks carrying the others along, they are sent a series of in-depth questionnaires. Between rounds, each receives controlled feedback on the group's opinions and may then revise his answer. The method, born to forecast the impact of technology on warfare, would later be used for technological forecasting, health and education.
Il fait connaître la méthode Delphi, enc: It made the Delphi method known, still used to get experts working together.
Ses auteurs trouvaient le nom de Delphi,: Its authors found the name Delphi, borrowed from the oracle, a bit too "occult".
Des experts anonymes qui se corrigent. V: Anonymous experts who correct themselves. You are anonymous and you don't correct yourself.
Dans cet article de l'American Journal o: In this article in the American Journal of Sociology, the sociologist Mark Granovetter starts from a survey of how professional and technical workers in a Massachusetts town found their jobs. Those who found one through a contact mostly got it through people they saw occasionally or rarely, not through close friends. Granovetter draws a simple idea from this: close friends form tight clusters where everyone knows the same things, and it is weak ties, mere acquaintances, that build bridges between these clusters. Without them, whole groups would not be connected at all.
C'est l'un des articles les plus influen: It is one of the most influential and most cited articles in sociology.
L'article est né de la thèse de Granovet: The article grew out of Granovetter's thesis on job searching, defended at Harvard in 1970.
Vos liens faibles vous trouvent du trava: Your weak ties find you work. Your strong ties with me give you some.
Le politiste Robert Axelrod cherche comm: The political scientist Robert Axelrod asks how cooperation can arise among egoists, without a central authority. He organizes tournaments in which programs play the repeated prisoner's dilemma: on each move, each can cooperate or betray. The winner is the simplest strategy, tit for tat, submitted by Anatol Rapoport: cooperate first, then return the favor. The successful strategies are nice, retaliate when betrayed, forgive quickly and do not try to beat the other. The book also shows that cooperation depends on the chances of meeting again, and that a small group of cooperators can take root among cheaters.
Il montre, avec la théorie des jeux, com: It shows, with game theory, how cooperation can emerge without a leader.
Le livre prolonge un article écrit en 19: The book extends an article written in 1981 with the evolutionary biologist W. D. Hamilton.
Donnant-donnant : vous révisez, je suis: Tit for tat: you revise, I'm pleasant. You skip, I pay you back.

Pendant près de vingt ans, de 1984 à 200: For nearly twenty years, from 1984 to 2003, the psychologist Philip Tetlock ran small forecasting tournaments. His participants were 284 experts: government officials, professors, journalists. He collected about 28,000 predictions about the future, then waited to see what happened. The verdict, published in 2005 by Princeton University Press, was harsh: the experts often did only slightly better than chance, and generally worse than simple extrapolation rules, especially at three to five years. Tetlock distinguishes two styles: hedgehogs, attached to one big idea, are wrong more often, especially in their own field. The book leads straight to the Good Judgment Project.
Il est le premier à mesurer, sur des mil: It was the first to measure, over thousands of forecasts, what an expert's opinion is really worth.
Le livre reçoit en 2008 le prix Grawemey: In 2008 the book received the Grawemeyer Award from the University of Louisville, for ideas improving world order.
Vingt-huit mille prédictions d'experts,: Twenty-eight thousand expert predictions, barely better than chance. Yours, I no longer even count.
Eric Raymond oppose deux manières d'écri: Eric Raymond contrasts two ways of writing software. In the cathedral, a small team works out of sight and releases only finished versions. In the bazaar, like Linus Torvalds's Linux kernel, the code is open to all, released early and often, and hundreds of volunteers test and fix it. Raymond draws from this Linus's law: given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow. First presented as a talk in 1997, then published as a book in 1999, the essay weighed in Netscape's decision to open its browser's code and launch the Mozilla project.
Il explique pourquoi un logiciel écrit p: It explains why software written by a crowd of volunteers can be more reliable.
Le patron de Netscape, Jim Barksdale, a: Netscape's CEO, Jim Barksdale, cited the essay as a major influence in opening his browser's code.
Avec assez d'yeux, tous les bugs se voie: Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are visible. With my two eyes, I see all your mistakes.
Le journaliste James Surowiecki rassembl: The journalist James Surowiecki gathers examples where a large group of ordinary people judges better than its experts. He opens his book with the Plymouth fair of 1906, where the median of 800 guesses of an ox's weight came out almost exactly right. He covers markets, betting, TV game shows and scientific research. But he insists on the conditions: the crowd is wise only if its members think diversely and independently, with local information, and if some mechanism gathers their opinions. When everyone copies everyone else, the crowd becomes a herd and goes wrong in chorus.
Il a popularisé l'idée de sagesse des fo: It popularized the idea of the wisdom of crowds and its conditions.
Au jeu Qui veut gagner des millions ?, l: On Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, the audience was right 91% of the time, against 65% for the "expert friends" called on the phone, even though it was probably asked easier questions.
La foule est sage si elle est diverse. V: A crowd is wise if it is diverse. You are alone. Do the math.
